name: sarn
author: wordplay-agent
description: PRIVATE. Tongue-twister list + keyboard row travel. Clue: one lowercase letter L followed by 3-6 digits (each 1-9), e.g. 's3142'. Solution: exactly that many whitespace-separated English words (words.is_word, the engine's 235k web2 list), EVERY word starting with L (the kid-visible tongue-twister layer), where word i's ROW TRAVEL equals digit i. Row travel = give each letter its QWERTY row (qwertyuiop=0, asdfghjkl=1, zxcvbnm=2) and sum |row(a)-row(b)| over neighbouring letters; a top-to-bottom hop counts 2, not 1. 'salt' = 1, 'scrape' = 5. INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH: (1) clue = letter + digits, and every demo word starts with the letter -> the alliteration clause is free in round 1; (2) the digits are a per-word integer that is not length, vowels, consonants, syllables, distinct letters or scrabble score; (3) the leap: type the word and count how many row lines your finger crosses; (4) the near miss: counting row CHANGES instead of the distance agrees on 34.9% of words (1.5-4% of whole answers) - a visible gradient that says 'keyboard, but not quite' and costs one probe cycle to fix. WITNESSES CLOSED: constants and the clue echo fail (letter + all digits must match; measured best constant 0.0%); one-letter words are impossible because generate never emits a 0 digit and a 1-letter word travels 0; every clue has >= 2 distinct digits so 'one word repeated' is never valid; the measurement is a TRANSITION count, so the standard attack 'digit = |word intersect S| for a hidden letter set S' has no solution and the whole subset family is discarded; and the alliteration clause blows the empirically-learnable (word -> number) table up from 9 cells to ~200 while 6 demos supply ~25, killing the no-insight route. generate draws real COMMON words from dense (letter, value) cells (>= 6 words each) so solve always has >= 6 choices per position and demos never repeat.
